reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with a measurable-space structure equal to its Borel structure, and every real polynomial p, let phi:R->R be the actual function phi(z)=p.eval(z). Let gamma1 be gaussianReal(0,1), the actual one-dimensional standard Gaussian, and gammaE be stdGaussian(E), the actual centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian on E. Then there exists a witness hbase of MemLp(phi,2,gamma1). For that witness define b=norm(hbase.toLp(phi))+1. This b is strictly positive. Moreover, there exists a single family hfeature witnessing, for every w in the subtype U={w:E | norm(w)=1}, MemLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x)),2,gammaE). For that family, for every w in U, both norm((hfeature(w)).toLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x))))=norm(hbase.toLp(phi)) and norm((hfeature(w)).toLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x))))<=b hold, with the feature norm under gammaE and base norm under gamma1. MemLp and all of the membership witnesses are conclusions rather than supplied integrability assumptions; they assert almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm of the displayed actual functions. The toLp constructions are the genuine equivalence classes of those fixed functions, not choices of alternative functions or laws. The same base witness, the b defined from its norm, and the single feature-witness family serve every unit direction; b does not vary with w. Semantically the base norm and b depend only on p and the fixed gamma1 law, not on the witness proof, E, or direction. The exact equality identifies the norm of each polynomial ridge with the one-dimensional norm, whereas the inequality supplies the larger common positive bound b. Since norms are nonnegative, the definition also gives b>=1, although the explicit positivity claim is b>0. No nonzero polynomial, positive degree, or positive-dimension assumption is imposed. If p is the zero polynomial, phi and every ridge are zero, their L2 norms are zero, and b=1. If E has dimension zero, there are no unit vectors, so the feature-membership family and its universally quantified equality and bound are vacuous, while the base membership and positivity of b remain asserted. No analogous statement for nonunit weights or a global pointwise bound on the polynomial features is claimed.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with Borel measurable structure; real polynomial p; actual polynomial-evaluation function phi; actual Gaussian laws gamma1=gaussianReal 0 1 and gammaE=stdGaussian E; base L2-membership witness hbase; norm-defined real b; unit-weight subtype U; ridge functions x->p.eval(inner_product(w,x)); and one universally indexed family hfeature of ridge L2-membership witnesses.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. The norm topology supplies the Borel structure. No explicit CompleteSpace or positive-dimensional/nontrivial-space hypothesis appears; finite dimensionality over R entails completeness. p:Polynomial R is arbitrary. phi:R->R uses literal finite polynomial evaluation. gamma1 is the one-dimensional N(0,1) probability and gammaE is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian on E. Weights range exactly over {w:E | norm(w)=1}; x ranges over all E. Base classes are in real L2(gamma1), ridge classes in real L2(gammaE), and b is real.
quantifiers: For every E with the stated structures and every p, define phi. Existentially quantify hbase:MemLp(phi,2,gamma1). Only then define b=norm(hbase.toLp(phi))+1. For that base witness and b, conclude b>0 and existentially quantify one family hfeature:forall w in U, MemLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x)),2,gammaE). For that same family quantify every w in U and assert both exact norm equality and the common bound. The hfeature proof family depends on E,p and its unit argument, while the fixed functions themselves were already specified; hbase and hfeature are proofs, not random-variable choices.
assumptions: Only the listed algebraic, normed, inner-product, finite-dimensional, and Borel measurable-space structures, and an arbitrary given real polynomial p. Neither scalar Gaussian L2 membership, ridge Gaussian L2 membership, positivity of b, equality of norms, nor uniform norm boundedness is assumed: all are concluded. No restriction on polynomial degree or coefficients, no nonzero-polynomial premise, no positive dimension, and no separate unit-vector existence premise is supplied. The individual weights in the quantified subtype satisfy norm(w)=1 by their type.
conclusion: There is hbase proving genuine scalar L2 membership of z->p.eval(z) under gamma1. With b equal to its L2 norm plus exactly 1, b>0. There is one family of genuine L2-membership witnesses for all x->p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) under gammaE, indexed by every exact unit vector w. For each such w, its L2(gammaE) norm equals the base L2(gamma1) norm exactly and is at most b. This is a proof-dependent syntactic construction of equivalence classes whose mathematical functions and norms are independent of the choice of membership proof.
scopes: The base law is the fixed one-dimensional standard Gaussian; the ridge law is the actual standard Gaussian of the given E. Both norms use their own displayed measures. The unit restriction is exact and no claim for weights of norm below or above 1 is asserted. A single b is defined before the feature-witness family and universal unit-weight quantifier, so the bound is uniform over all unit directions. L2 norms concern almost-everywhere equivalence classes rather than pointwise bounds; no pointwise boundedness of polynomial evaluation is concluded. If E is zero dimensional the unit subtype is empty and the feature assertions are vacuous, but the scalar base existence and b>0 are still required. The zero polynomial is allowed and gives base and feature norm zero with b=1. There is no independent parameter-law assumption, finite-particle scope, or derivative conclusion.
constant_dependencies: The bound is exactly b=norm_{L2(gaussianReal 0 1)}(p.eval)+1, not an unspecified existential constant. Its positive additive slack is exactly 1, so b>=1 and therefore b>0 even for p=0. The feature norm equality is exact with multiplicative factor 1 and has no dimension or direction factor. Mathematically b depends only on p and the fixed one-dimensional standard Gaussian, independent of E, w, and membership proof. The statement gives the non-strict feature bound <=b and no closed-form coefficient or degree estimate for the base norm.
